fundamental.thesis: Aditya Birla Real Estate (ABREL) is a mid-cap residential developer, operating through Birla Estates, that is moving away from its legacy pulp and paper business; it is expanding in MMR, NCR, Bengaluru and Pune, including the premium Pune projects announced on 2026-10-23. The latest extracted official quarter is Q1 FY27: total revenue rose 30.6% YoY to ₹205.7 cr, reversing the -43.0% fall in Q2 FY26, but continuing operations lost ₹67.0 cr after tax versus a ₹47.3 cr loss a year earlier, with a real-estate segment margin of -37%. Reported profit was propped up only by ₹32.4 cr from the discontinued paper business, and the Q2 FY27 results filed on 2026-10-26 have not yet been extracted, so the yfinance Q2 print (₹524 cr revenue, ₹83 cr PAT) cannot be verified. The sector card says developers should be judged on pre-sales, collections, net debt and launch pipeline rather than P/E, but none of these figures are in today's data; on the fallback yardstick the stock trades at 3.9x book with a negative ROE of -8.9% and near the bottom of its 52-week range (17%), which I grade fair rather than cheap until booking momentum can be checked. The biggest risks are a core business that keeps losing money while debt is elevated, and inconsistent balance-sheet data: reported debt-to-equity ranges from 1.57x to 5.76x, and ₹3,718 cr of preference shares need clarification.

fundamental.thesis: Anant Raj is an NCR-focused mid-cap developer that is building a data-centre and cloud business alongside its residential projects; a Board-approved demerger of the data-centre arm into a subsidiary is awaiting NCLT approval. Growth has slowed sharply: H1 FY27 revenue was ₹1,293 cr (+5.7% YoY), down from +24-26% through FY26, and the implied Q2 FY27 revenue of about ₹662 cr was only about +5% YoY. PAT still grew faster than revenue, reaching ₹306 cr (+15.8%), because EBITDA margin widened to 32.3% from about 27-29%. On the sector card's yardstick valuation looks fair: P/E is not meaningful for developers and pre-sales/bookings data was not provided, so I graded on P/B 3.2x against an annualised ROE of about 10-11% (a rich pairing) and EV/EBITDA 28.6x (P63 vs the broad market), offset by a forward P/E of 18.5x and P/B at P36. The biggest risk is weak cash conversion: H1 operating cash flow was only about ₹32 cr against ₹306 cr of PAT (0.10x), and FY26 free cash flow was -₹693 cr, so reported profits are not yet turning into cash while capex and inventory of about ₹1,507 cr keep rising.

fundamental.thesis: Brigade Enterprises is a Bengaluru-centred midcap developer with residential, leasing and hospitality arms, and its 67.5%-margin leasing book gives it a recurring income base its larger luxury peers mostly lack. H1FY27 revenue fell 13.2% YoY to ₹2,312 cr as real estate segment revenue dropped 26.6% to ₹1,374 cr, while PAT rose 32.7% to ₹436 cr (18.9% margin, up from 11.8% in Q3FY26). That profit is weakly backed by cash: CFO/PAT is only 0.42x and FCF just ₹79 cr. The sector card says P/E is meaningless for developers and the right yardstick is pre-sales, collections and net debt, but no pre-sales or collections data was provided. The live P/B (30.5x), EV/EBITDA (143.6x) and 31% dividend yield are plainly data errors (net worth of ₹7,155 cr against a ₹20,830 cr market cap implies P/B near 2.9x), so I grade valuation 'fair' on that implied book multiple and net debt/EBITDA of 2.1x, with low confidence. The biggest risks are the falling core residential revenue and the legal overhang: a revoked environmental clearance on a Chennai project and a disputed ₹860 cr JDA deposit in arbitration.

At 16.3× trailing P/E — a 33.7% discount to the IT sector peer median of 24.7× and cheapest in sector on forward P/E at 13.4× — TCS screens unambiguously cheap versus both sector peers and the benchmark range of 22–30×, with a pristine balance sheet (CFO/PAT 0.94×, FCF ₹23,768 cr in H1) providing a durable floor; the P/E yardstick is used here as primary per the asset-light IT services model, and EV/EBITDA at 11.1× (P17 in sector vs median 14.7×) corroborates the cheap read. The central risk is AI-led productivity deflation continuing to compress legacy T&M revenues in constant-currency terms: if INR stabilises from current weakness, CC growth likely reverts to near-zero or negative, the INR acceleration collapses, and the re-rating catalyst disappears, leaving TCS cheap but with no near-term earnings growth to close the discount.

The trend data is internally inconsistent and cannot be trusted for the latest quarter: the Q1FY27 row is blank, and quarterly revenue of ₹5,215–5,398 cr in Q2–Q3FY26 against ₹21,097 cr in Q4FY26 (+21.9% YoY, PAT ₹3,382 cr, -9.8% YoY) looks like mixed reporting entities, so the pre-computed 'accelerating' signal is unreliable. The one clean KPI, ARPU, has been essentially flat at ₹256 → ₹259 → ₹257 over three quarters, which means the premiumisation story is stalling until the next tariff hike. On the sector card's yardstick (EV/EBITDA, India mobile norm 9–12×), the stock is fair at 10.54×; it trades near its 52-week low (15% of range), 90-day EPS revisions are slightly negative (-1.5%), and the trailing P/E of 40.7× is less useful here. fundamental.thesis: Axis Bank is India's third-largest private-sector bank, with a large corporate and wholesale book, a growing retail franchise and a consolidated life-insurance associate (Axis Max Life). In Q2FY27, total income rose 14.8% YoY to ₹45,674 cr and PAT rose 39.4% to ₹7,705 cr. Revenue growth has picked up from about +4% (H1FY26) to +7% (Q1FY27) to +15%, and loan growth has risen from 11.9% to 19.3%, but the PAT jump is flattered by a weak Q2FY26 base (₹5,528 cr), and the PAT margin slipped from 17.7% in Q1 to 16.9%. On the lender yardstick from the sector card (P/B against sustainable ROE), a P/B of 1.83x for a TTM ROE of 13.2% is fair: it is above the peer median of 1.5x (P64), while trailing P/E of 15.0x is about 11% below peers (P43). That fits a bank whose asset quality has improved (GNPA down from 1.46% to 1.23%) but whose returns are only moderate. The biggest risk is that loans are now growing faster than deposits: the loan-to-deposit ratio is a stretched 98.7%, credit cost has risen from 0.20% to 0.72%, and provision coverage is slipping (70.5% to 70.0%). Together these point to future funding-cost and NIM pressure, and the extracted NIM readings (3.42% in Q1 vs 2.32% in Q2) conflict too much to confirm the NIM recovery the sector card expects.

fundamental.thesis: Sun Pharma is India's largest drugmaker. It holds about 8.5% of the India formulations market (No. 1), and its global specialty (Innovative Medicines) business now makes up about 22% of sales, so its growth no longer depends mainly on US generics. In Q1FY27 revenue rose 10.1% YoY to ₹15,184 cr and reported PAT rose 26.9% to ₹2,895 cr, a 19.1% margin. Some of the PAT jump comes from the lower tax rate it moved to, and it is despite ₹204 cr of one-off Organon and labour-code charges. Underneath, the business is weaker: EBITDA grew only 2.7%, the EBITDA margin fell to 28.9% from about 31-32% in FY26, India grew 16% but US formulations shrank 9.7% in USD as lenalidomide competition hits, and the trend table mixes quarterly, half-year and nine-month figures, so the 'accelerating' revenue signal is not reliable. On valuation, a trailing P/E of 37.4x sits inside the 28-40x pharma range and near the peer median (P54), while EV/EBITDA of 24.2x is 13% above the peer median (P62); judged on P/E and EV/EBITDA against peers, the stock is fairly valued, with only modest support from the 27.7x forward P/E and slightly rising estimates. The biggest risk is the $11.75B Organon acquisition: closing it in Q4FY27 turns a net-cash balance sheet (about ₹26,000 cr of net cash in FY25, FY26 debt/equity 0.05) into a leveraged one with integration risk. This comes while the US generics base is shrinking and the US review of tariffs on generics is still pending.

fundamental.thesis: UltraTech is India's largest cement maker with 210.1 mtpa of capacity, and it benefits from an industry where it and Adani now control roughly 45% of capacity, which supports pricing discipline. In Q2FY27 revenue grew 18.9% YoY to ₹23,024 cr, up from 15.8% in Q1, and PAT rose 21.3% to ₹1,501 cr on 12.9% volume growth. Margins fell sharply from Q1, though: EBITDA margin dropped from 20.9% to 16.6% and PAT margin from 10.6% to 6.5%, and EBITDA per tonne fell from ₹1,214 to ₹974 (still up ₹60 YoY). The cause is cost inflation, with fuel up 14% and packing bags up 30% on the crude spike, against realisation growth of only 2%. Part of this is the normal monsoon-quarter slowdown, and H1 cash conversion is solid at 1.68x CFO/PAT. Using the cement yardstick (EBITDA per tonne plus peer multiples, since live EV/EBITDA was not available), the stock looks fair. Its 39.6x trailing P/E is close to the sector median of 37.3x (P53 among peers), but the 4.5x P/B is rich for a 10.6% ROE, and the 25.1x forward P/E rests on estimates that have been cut 11–13% in the last 30 days. The biggest risk is that crude above $103 keeps fuel and packing costs high while realisations barely rise, so per-tonne profits stay squeezed and the stock de-rates as analysts keep trimming earnings.

NTPC is India's largest power generator. It earns a regulated return on equity (around 15.5%) on the plants it commissions, plus a growing renewables arm, so its earnings follow the pace of new capacity rather than power prices. In Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue was ₹51,142 cr (+7.0% YoY) and PAT ₹6,896 cr (+12.9% YoY, 13.5% margin), a pickup after FY26 revenue was flat (-0.4%) with PAT up 15.0%. The trend table's 'accelerating/expanding' signals are unreliable because they compare single quarters against cumulative half-year, 9-month and full-year totals, so I rely only on the Q1 FY27 YoY print and the FY26 annual figures. On EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for this capital-intensive business, NTPC trades at 8.4x against a peer median of 11.6x, and its trailing P/E of 11.9x is the cheapest in its peer group (-18.8% vs median), so I grade it cheap vs peers. Two caveats temper that: the 11.9x P/E sits inside the 10-18x utilities benchmark, and the peer median is inflated by the richly valued Adani names. The forward P/E of 12.8x is above the trailing figure, which implies a slight earnings dip ahead. Q2 FY27 results are due 31 Oct and are not yet reflected here. The balance sheet is leveraged (debt/equity roughly 1.18x) and the board has approved a further ₹12,000 cr NCD raise.

fundamental.thesis: Titan is India's largest organised jewellery retailer (Tanishq) with watches, eyewear and other premium lifestyle brands. The only quarter with full numbers in our filings is Q3FY26, showing revenue of ₹24,592 cr (+40.0% YoY) and PAT of ₹1,684 cr (+61.0% YoY, 6.8% PAT margin). Every later period through Q2FY27 is blank, so we cannot tell whether growth is speeding up or slowing down. Q2FY27 results are due at the 5 Nov 2026 board meeting. On valuation, we used the sector card's yardstick for premium discretionary franchises (normal band 60–100×) alongside EV/EBITDA. A trailing P/E of 74.3× and forward P/E of 49.4× sit inside the card's premium band, so we grade it fair overall, though not cheap. Against peers it is clearly rich: EV/EBITDA of 48.1× is 119% above the sector median (P94) and P/B of 24.0× is at P90. That premium is partly earned by a 37% ROE, and the peer median is pulled down by lower-multiple auto names. The biggest risk is that a growth disappointment at a 74× multiple can trigger the 25–40% de-rating the sector card warns about. That risk is higher in a risk-off market with rising crude and a falling gold price, which can hurt inventory gains and jewellery margins.

fundamental.thesis: ONGC is India's dominant PSU upstream oil & gas producer, contributing roughly 65% of domestic crude output; its economics are policy-administered, with crude realisation the primary earnings lever and a permanent government-interference discount structurally embedded in the multiple. Revenue has declined consistently over five periods — from -0.4% YoY in FY25 to -9.4% in Q1FY26 before recovering to -3.9% for full-year FY26 (₹132,508 cr), with PAT falling 7.6% YoY to ₹32,894 cr and PAT margin contracting 101 bps to 24.8%; the trajectory is one of sustained negative momentum, though CFO/PAT of 2.05× confirms these earnings are genuinely cash-backed. Using the Sector Card's mandated yardstick of trailing P/E + yield for PSU upstream, the 8.04× P/E sits comfortably mid-range within the 6–10× policy-priced band and EV/EBITDA of 4.56× is 25% below the sector median (P33 vs peers), while forward P/E at 6.08× (P0 — cheapest in sector) implies the market is pricing in a crude-driven earnings recovery — together this grades 'fair' rather than cheap, in keeping with the Sector Card's caution against calling a policy-constrained name cheap. The central risk is windfall-tax re-imposition or administered price caps during an inflationary or election cycle, which would neutralise the current crude tailwind ($89.72 and rising) just as realisations should be expanding.

fundamental.thesis: Bajaj Finserv is a financial holding company whose value comes mainly from its stake in Bajaj Finance, India's largest consumer lender, plus its life and general insurance subsidiaries and newer AMC, health and broking businesses. In Q1 FY27, consolidated total income grew 19.2% YoY to ₹42,037 cr, up from +12.6% a year earlier. However, PAT attributable to owners grew only 12% to ₹3,132 cr, which works out to a margin of about 7.5% versus 7.9% in Q1 FY26. The 'expanding margin' trajectory signal is an artifact: the ₹6,297 cr headline figure includes minority shareholders, while the prior-year figures in the table appear to be attributable-only. Within the group, Bajaj Finance is strong (PAT +28%, AUM +24%, Gross NPA down to 0.96% from 1.24%, provision coverage up to 60%), Bajaj Life VNB rose 87%, but Bajaj General's PAT fell 27% as its combined ratio worsened to 104.7%. On the lender yardstick the sector card prescribes (P/B against sustainable ROE), a P/B of 3.5x for an ROE of 14.6% is a premium (P73 vs peers, sector median P/B 2.0x). That is partly justified by the quality of Bajaj Finance and offset by the stock sitting at only 21% of its 52-week range, so I grade it fair rather than cheap. The biggest near-term swing factor is Q2 FY27 results on 3 Nov 2026, eight days away, where continued general-insurance underwriting losses and cash burn in the emerging businesses could drag on owner-level earnings growth.

books.title: Fundamental grades → rules
books.hypothesis: Strong growers that are not yet decelerating, held whole and long: the one filter with measured forward information (+2.5 pp at 60 sessions, +5.6 pp at 120 vs the equal-weight universe in the point-in-time study), alone — kept at target weight and re-qualified every 120 sessions.

rules.eligible: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes)
rules.rank: revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass growth == strong, risk != high, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, sentiment bearish with conviction >= 0.5, or the 120-session review failing (growth not strong, risk high or decelerating); between reviews never for decelerating, never for timing, never on missing data
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session

books.title: Fundamental grades ∩ momentum, 200-day overlay

rules.signal: monthly — first session on/after the month's last weekday (start date counts)
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); between signal dates the book holds except on a flip, when survivors are rebalanced (no entries or exits)
rules.universe: close > own 200-day SMA, 12-1 momentum known AND the shared fundamental filter (growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes))
rules.exit: rank > 60, close < 200-day SMA, fundamental deterioration (growth -> weak / risk -> high)
rules.entry: new entries wait until the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; holdings are never sold for timing

books.title: Technical pullback in uptrends
books.hypothesis: Technicals the right way round in a mean-reverting tape: buy the dip in a leader and give it time — a 10-session minimum hold and a 20-session cap keep the edge from being traded away in charges.

rules.universe: close > 200-day SMA and 12-1 momentum in the top 20% of names with momentum
rules.entry: 5-session return <= -4% or close < 20-day SMA; ranked by momentum (strongest first)
rules.hold: minimum 10 sessions from the fill (the stop still applies)
rules.exit: after the minimum hold, close >= 20-day SMA or 20 sessions held; -10% from the fill price at any time

books.title: Macro + fundamental, sector rotation
books.hypothesis: Top-down sector timing adds to the bottom-up filter (strong, non-decelerating growers). Judged against b6_neutral — the same construction with every tilt at 1.0 — by more than the random band, plus the sector-call scorecard at one month (>= 60% hit, >= +1 pp per call, model months only); at least 6-8 monthly calls before any judgement, two quarters the floor.

rules.signal: monthly — first session of the calendar month (or the first run after it); one sector_strategist call; none on other days or in a dry run
rules.tilt: per sector in [0.5, 2.0], clamped; sum of |change| per signal capped at 1.0; weights normalised to 1 over sectors with eligible names (neutral = equal share); fallback = the standing tilt (neutral at first)

rules.judge: Book 6 minus b6_neutral (the same construction, every tilt 1.0, zero LLM) must exceed the random band; scorecard at 1m >= 60% hit and >= +1 pp per call, over- and under-weights each above their own null (~45% / ~55%), model months only; at least 6-8 monthly calls before any judgement (two quarters is the floor)
